title: Choose the look for Nadir — bolder hand
question: Bolder forms, each translated to your white, clean, card-grid brief. The dice put the Signal Bench first. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Signal Bench
options.lineage: Lab oscilloscopes and their printed screen captures, translated to white
options.thesis: Every stock is a signal: each card is a small scope screen, and a fall is read in divisions of that stock's normal swing.
options.viewport: A bench header with the trigger controls (fell at least X, grew at least Y), a status strip showing which feeds are still arming, then a grid of scope cards, each trace frozen with the crash window bracketed.
options.risk: If the graticule and readouts get busy, it tips back into the chaos you rejected; the grid must stay faint and the cards spare.

raised.raise: States stamp themselves in place (earnings, shock, market-wide) instead of adding new UI.
Every card is deep-linkable, and Back retraces exactly where you were.
The detail panel steps through the fall in numbered stages, one idea each.
Corner brackets snap around the focused card for keyboard navigation.

options.label: The Ticket Wallet
options.lineage: Jet-age airline ticket wallets and coupons
options.thesis: Each fallen stock is a coupon in this week's wallet, with carbon-copy numerals and stamped states.
options.viewport: A wallet header with the week, then coupon cards with ruled fields: company, fall, record, and a stamp for the cause.
options.case: Holds clarity and white mode well; loses narrowly on audience fit, since travel is not investing.
options.risk: Reads as a theme if the coupon chrome outweighs the numbers.

options.label: The HyperCard Stack
options.lineage: 1987 HyperCard stacks, one-bit black on white
options.thesis: A shoebox of black-and-white cards, one per stock, linked by buttons you can follow and retrace.
options.viewport: A menu bar, then a grid of fixed-proportion cards with painted buttons; opening one flips to its card.
options.case: Strong on white-mode and card clarity; loses on audience fit, as pixel type feels retro rather than clean.
options.risk: Nostalgia can overpower the data; pixel fonts tire the eye.

options.label: Orizuru Crane
options.thesis: One vermilion sheet folded in 32 numbered steps.
options.viewport: A red folding sheet with numbered steps.
options.case: Loses both: a full red ground fights white mode and says nothing about markets.
options.kept: Numbered stages in the detail panel.

options.label: Mesophotic Deep Dive
options.thesis: A descent down a reef wall as a depth axis.
options.viewport: A vertical dive profile with depth readouts.
options.case: Loses both: dark blue ground breaks the white brief; depth-as-drawdown is a stretch.
options.kept: One vertical axis ruling the detail chart.

options.label: Camcorder Viewfinder
options.thesis: An on-screen display framing live content.
options.case: Loses on clarity: HUD overlays compete with the numbers.

canonCard.label: The broker-app standard
canonCard.thesis: What stock apps ship: white cards, green and red numbers, system font, executed carefully.
canonCard.viewport: A watchlist-style card grid with ticker, price and change.
canonCard.risk: Clean but interchangeable with every broker app.
